In a video shared by Screen International on X, Abraham said: “Since this festival started, Israel killed at least six Palestinian children in Gaza.” 

“A three-year-old girl at a school that was bombed, a seven-year-old with her father in the car and two sisters at home sleeping,” he said.

“And, you know the Israeli intelligence officers we spoke with talk to us how this mass killing is systemic, not by accident but by design. Actions of murder and policies that are based on total dehumanisation of Palestinians.

“I want you to know that this truth has been documented from the first day thanks to Palestinian journalists. Their voices were silenced and denied. We believe that the denial of the crime is what helps it persist. And that is why it is really, really important for us that Israelis watch this film,” he added.

OCHA: West Bank schooling disrupted by displacement, pending demolitions

More than 830,000 Palestinian boys and girls returned to school this week in the occupied West Bank, but thousands face continued disruption to their education, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

In a statement, OCHA said more than 4,000 students among those returning to school had been displaced from refugee camps in the northern West Bank and have not been allowed to return.

Schooling has also been affected by the closure of six UNRWA schools in occupied East Jerusalem by Israeli authorities, OCHA said.

In Area C of the West Bank, 10 schools serving more than 360 students remain abandoned after the communities they served were displaced by recurrent settler attacks and related access restrictions.

Meanwhile, 84 schools remain under pending demolition or stop-work orders, putting the continued education of nearly 13,000 students at risk, according to OCHA.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Bahrain won't attend meeting on Hormuz in Oman
item.description:
Bahrain won't attend meeting on Hormuz in Oman

Bahrain has announced it would not participate in the meeting scheduled for Monday in Oman between Iran and Gulf states regarding the Strait of Hormuz, according to AFP.

In a statement, Bahrain's foreign ministry said that Bahrain "will not be a party to any collective meeting involving Iran prior to the restoration of diplomatic relations between the two countries".

Bahrain cut diplomatic ties with Iran in 2016 alongside Saudi Arabia during an earlier crisis between the regional rivals. While Riyadh restored ties in 2023, Manama is yet to do so.

Pointing to attacks on infrastructure across the Gulf, the ministry said that security and stability in the region "cannot be preserved through a policy of appeasement" and called for Hormuz to be open without "discrimination, fees or permits". 

Iran's foreign ministry had said there would be a meeting on Monday hosted by Muscat where the future of the strait, vital for global oil and gas flows, would be negotiated.

Bahrain emphasised that "dialogue cannot be based on ignoring realities," noting that, during the war, it had been subjected to attacks launched by Iran that targeted its infrastructure and civilian assets.

Reporting by AFP

item.description:
Palestine welcomes Brics declaration calling for two-state solution

Palestinian ministry of foreign affairs and expatriates has welcomed the Brics declaration calling for a two-state solution to the Palestine issue.

In a statement, the ministry said it particularly welcomed the declaration's rejection of attempts to forcibly displace the Palestinian people from their land, including Jerusalem and its call for an end to the Israeli occupation.

The ministry welcomed "its reaffirmation of the two-state solution; its support for the full membership of the State of Palestine in the United Nations; and its support for an independent, sovereign and viable Palestinian state along the June 4, 1967 borders, with Jerusalem as its capital".

It also welcomed the declaration's support for UNRWA and its mandate, as well as its call to protect holy sites and ensure access to them in Jerusalem, protect the Palestinian people, and guarantee unhindered humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip.

The ministry praised these positions as consistent with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, stressing the need to translate them into practical and concrete steps.

item.description:
Several Palestinians detained, two injured during raids by Israeli forces, settlers

Several Palestinians were detained and a few others injured in raids by Israeli forces and settlers in the occupied West Bank. Here is a recap of some of these incidents reported by Wafa:

* Israeli forces detained eight Palestinians during raids on Jenin city and several towns and villages across the governorate on Sunday. 

* Two children, 15-year-old Majed Maher Abdel Fattah and 14-year-old Ahmad Mahmoud Shokeh, were detained during a raid on their home in Bethlehem city.

*Israeli forces tightened military measures at the Atara checkpoint, north of Ramallah, obstructing the movement of Palestinian vehicles and causing severe traffic congestion.

*A Palestinian man was injured by Israeli gunfire in Ras al-Amud area of Silwan, south of Al-Aqsa Mosque in the occupied Jerusalem.

*Israeli bulldozers on Saturday evening began levelling Palestinian-owned land and reopening blocked roads to facilitate the movement of Israeli settlers during their attacks on the village, according to Amin Abu Alia, head of the Al-Mughayyir Village Council.

*Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian homes in Yasuf village, east of the town of Salfit in the central West Bank.

* Israeli soldiers seized a bulldozer belonging to a Palestinian resident of the town of Bidya town, west of Salfit, while it was operating in the town.

*Israeli forces stormed the village of Muthallath al-Shuhada, south of Jenin, accompanied by detained teenager Omar Fadi Abu Murad. Soldiers raided his father’s home, as well as several homes belonging to his uncles, and ransacked them.

*A 68-year-old man suffered injuries to his back and chest, while a 14-year-old boy broke his hand during an Israeli raid on Marka, south of Jenin.

*Israeli forces arrested several Palestinians during raids across Jenin governorate, including in Deir Abu Daif and Faqqua, and carried out further searches in Zububa, al-Silah al-Harithiya and other areas.

*Two brothers were arrested in Tammun, south of Tubas, while Israeli forces also raided Tayasir.
Settlers attacked the outskirts of Burqa, east of Ramallah, throwing stones at homes and vehicles and damaging at least one car.

*In occupied East Jerusalem, a Palestinian man was forced to demolish five businesses he owned in the Wadi al-Joz industrial area after being threatened with heavy municipal fines.
